name: Hidden text direction controls
description: Hidden direction controls can make instructions or code appear in a different order from the order the computer reads.
source: Unicode UAX #9 explicit directional formatting characters: https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr9/

name: Invisible text characters
description: Invisible characters can conceal or separate instructions without changing how the text looks. They may also be legitimate language formatting.

name: Hidden Unicode tag characters
description: Unicode tags can carry text that is not visibly displayed. Review whether they are necessary for the package.
source: Unicode Tags block and default-ignorable characters: https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/UE0000.pdf

name: Invisible operators or separators
description: Invisible operators or separators can hide boundaries inside instructions. They may also be legitimate mathematical notation.
source: Unicode General Punctuation, invisible operators U+2061 through U+2064: https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U2000.pdf

name: Possible committed GitHub access token
description: The package contains text shaped like a GitHub personal access token. If real, it can grant access to repositories; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule github-pat; adapted with token boundaries and an all-X placeholder exclusion: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/github.go

name: Possible committed GitHub OAuth token
description: The package contains text shaped like a GitHub OAuth token. If real, it can expose a connected account; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule github-oauth; adapted with token boundaries and an all-X placeholder exclusion: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/github.go

name: Possible committed GitHub application token
description: The package contains text shaped like a GitHub application token. If real, it can expose an application or its repositories; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule github-app-token; adapted with token boundaries and an all-X placeholder exclusion: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/github.go

name: Possible committed private key
description: The package contains a private-key header. If key material follows it, it could enable impersonation or decryption of private data.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule private-key; adapted to detect the header even without a complete key body: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/privatekey.go

name: Possible committed AWS access key ID
description: The package contains an AWS access key identifier. If its matching secret is exposed too, it can grant access to cloud resources; the identifier is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule aws-access-token; adapted with ASCII token boundaries, the upstream EXAMPLE exclusion, and uniform-placeholder rejection instead of an entropy filter: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/aws.go

name: Possible committed Slack bot token
description: The package contains text shaped like a Slack bot token. If real, it can grant access to a workspace through that bot; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule slack-bot-token; adapted with ASCII token boundaries (the upstream entropy filter is not applied): https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/slack.go

name: Possible committed Slack user token
description: The package contains text shaped like a Slack user token. If real, it can allow someone to act as that user in a workspace; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule slack-user-token; adapted with ASCII token boundaries (the upstream entropy filter is not applied): https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/slack.go

name: Possible committed Slack app token
description: The package contains text shaped like a Slack app-level token. If real, it can expose application access to a workspace; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule slack-app-token; adapted with ASCII digits and token boundaries (the upstream entropy filter is not applied): https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/slack.go

name: Possible committed Anthropic API key
description: The package contains text shaped like an Anthropic API key. If real, it can allow unauthorized API usage and charges; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule anthropic-api-key; adapted with explicit ASCII token boundaries: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/anthropic.go

name: Possible committed Anthropic admin API key
description: The package contains text shaped like an Anthropic admin API key. If real, it can expose administrative access to an organization; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule anthropic-admin-api-key; adapted with explicit ASCII token boundaries: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/anthropic.go

name: Possible committed OpenAI API key
description: The package contains text shaped like an OpenAI API key. If real, it can allow unauthorized API usage or account access; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule openai-api-key; retains legacy, project, service-account and admin formats, with explicit ASCII token boundaries (the upstream entropy filter is not applied): https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/openai.go

name: Possible committed Google API key
description: The package contains text shaped like a Google API key. If unrestricted, it can allow unauthorized service usage and charges; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule gcp-api-key; retains the upstream Firebase example allowlist, with explicit ASCII token boundaries and uniform-placeholder rejection instead of an entropy filter: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/gcp.go

name: Possible committed Stripe secret key
description: The package contains text shaped like a Stripe secret or restricted key. If real, it can expose payment operations or financial data; the value is redacted.
source: Gitleaks MIT-licensed rule stripe-access-token; retains secret and restricted test/live/prod keys, with explicit ASCII token boundaries and uniform-placeholder rejection instead of an entropy filter: https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/cmd/generate/config/rules/stripe.go
